minutes.headline: Budget Task Force heard a split-tax-rate comparison with Maynard and questions on underestimated local receipts; no votes taken.
minutes.summary: A member presented a data comparison of Lunenburg and Maynard (demographics, valuations, revenue, spending) to argue a split tax rate deserves discussion before the Select Board's November classification decision. The group also discussed conservative local receipts estimates, the levy left uncollected in FY24, and the link between local receipts and free cash for capital. CPA and a Marshall Park warrant update were briefly discussed; no formal votes were audible.

budget_items.what_was_said: Presenter showed local receipts were consistently underestimated versus actuals, with multi-year averages in the hundreds of thousands. He asked whether estimates should be less conservative.
The unlevied amount plus underestimated receipts was compared to the size of the recent override.
A finance official described a five-year average dropping the high and low, adjusted for market trend. Members noted no estimating methodology appears in the financial policy.
Discussion of free cash as a share of levy or general fund, with a rule of thumb given by a participant.
The former town manager's presentation showed local receipts estimates and an increase added to school department funding.
Free cash was transferred to the overlay account to cover abatements; the assessors can raise overlay to absorb unlevied room.
Presenter modelled Maynard's levy split on Lunenburg's FY24 levy; residential savings are a shift of burden, not new revenue.

budget_items.topic: Split rate impact on house vs business
budget_items.what_was_said: Carter illustrated a 1.1 shift saving a $500,000 house a small amount while a $500,000 business pays much more.
Recent override tax-rate impact was compared to the split rate savings.

budget_items.topic: Local receipts and free cash link
budget_items.what_was_said: Carter explained raising local receipts estimates reduces free cash available for capital and snow and ice.
CPA is a surcharge with state matching that has fallen over time, restricted to three spending categories.
A citizens petition for Marshall Park bonding was noted, with a project total and ARPA contribution mentioned.
Participants estimated annual debt service on a 20-year borrowing at an assumed rate.

what_happened.line: The Budget Task Force took no votes and agreed to submit a report for the November special town meeting warrant, with Tony to write the article.
A member presented a Lunenburg and Maynard comparison to argue that a split tax rate deserves discussion before the Select Board's November classification decision.
Members discussed local receipts being estimated below actuals, the levy left uncollected in FY24, and whether estimates should be less conservative.
A finance official described the receipts method as a five-year average adjusted for trend; members noted no estimating method appears in the financial policy.
The group planned to invite the capital planning chair to the September 30 meeting and to keep pressing the assessors for answers on CIP distribution and business flight.

why_it_matters: A split tax rate would shift the property tax burden between homes and businesses rather than raise new revenue, so it could change what a household's bill looks like at the Select Board's November classification decision.
Where local receipts are estimated affects how much free cash is left for capital projects and snow and ice, and how much room the town has before it asks voters for another override.
